title: `elicitation/create` (form)
description: A server request for structured user input, described by a restricted flat JSON Schema and answered with accept, decline or cancel.
question: Can a server ask the user a question through this framework?
why: Elicitation is the only client feature the 2026-07-28 index still recommends, and it is what lets a tool ask for the one missing detail instead of failing. A framework without it forces every server to guess or error.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: at 2026-07-28 the request arrives embedded in an `InputRequiredResult`. The adapter has no elicitation hook and calls tools through the MCP SDK's default `call_tool`, so the SDK's `Server returned InputRequiredResult` error reaches the caller as an `AgentsException` and nothing is answered.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): at 2026-07-28 the request arrives embedded in an `InputRequiredResult`. The client rejects any result with `resultType: "input_required"` ("multi round-trip requests are not supported yet"), so `execute` throws and nothing is answered. The registered `onElicitationRequest` handler never runs, so the probe cannot tell how it would answer. Kept `u` for that reason; `mrtr-input-required` carries the `n`.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0 at 2026-07-28: the server answers with `input_required`, and the MCP client the SDK builds tries to fulfil it itself, but no `elicitation/create` handler is registered on it and the SDK offers no option to add one. The call fails with `Cannot fulfil input request`, which the agent hands the model as tool-error text.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` builds its fastmcp `Client` with no elicitation handler and exposes no hook to add one, so form elicitation is refused.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy takes no elicitation handler. The server's request is answered only by a `elicitation_callback` registered on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: at 2026-07-28 `DefaultMcpClient` reads an `InputRequiredResult` and throws `Server sent inputRequests that the client cannot handle`, whatever is embedded. No hook answers it, so the tool call fails.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): mcptoolset has no elicitation option. A `mcp.ClientOptions.ElicitationHandler` set on the `*mcp.Client` the caller passes as `mcptoolset.Config.Client` answers the server's request, so it works, but only by configuring go-sdk rather than the toolset.
